bugs.error_message: Refuel step never actually refuels the vehicle; Repair step repairs correctly but afterward AutoDrive silently resumes driving to its previous target and WM never advances to the next step
bugs.root_cause: Two related AD-source-confirmed issues (read directly from FS25_AutoDrive/scripts): (1) startRefuelRoute routed through AutoDrive:StartDriving(vehicle, -1, -2, ...). Per ExternalInterface.lua's StartDriving, the -2 branch calls vehicle.ad.stateModule:getCurrentMode():start() (DriveToMode:start()) IMMEDIATELY, before any RefuelTask exists. If the vehicle has a stale vehicle.ad.stateModule:getFirstMarker() left over from an earlier normal AD step, DriveToMode:start() queues a DriveToDestinationTask toward that unrelated old destination instead of letting ADTaskModule's own RefuelIfNeeded() idle-tick check enqueue the real RefuelTask - Repair never had this problem because startRepairRoute bootstraps via vehicle:startAutoDrive() directly, bypassing StartDriving/DriveToMode:start() entirely. (2) Both RepairTask:finished() and RefuelTask:finished() (FS25_AutoDrive/scripts/Tasks/RepairTask.lua, RefuelTask.lua) call vehicle:stopAutoDrive() and then unconditionally vehicle.ad.stateModule:getCurrentMode():start() again right after. Since WM sets mode=MODE_DRIVETO before starting repair/refuel, this re-triggers DriveToMode:start(), which reactivates AD (isActive()=true) and, if a stale first-marker destination is set, immediately starts driving there - so WM's polling completion check (ADIntegration:isRouteComplete = 'not isActive()') never sees AD go inactive and the step never completes. Also confirmed vehicle.ad.callBackFunction (set by WM before StartDriving/startAutoDrive) is never invoked anywhere in this AD version - the callback-based completion path (ADIntegration.onRouteCompleteCallback) is dead code for all AD-tracked step types, not just refuel/repair; polling is the only mechanism that actually works.
bugs.fix: startRefuelRoute now bootstraps via vehicle:startAutoDrive() directly (mirrors startRepairRoute) instead of AutoDrive:StartDriving(-1,-2,...), avoiding the premature DriveToMode:start() call. Added ADIntegration:isRefuelRepairComplete(vehicle, flagName) which checks AD's own onRouteToRefuel/onRouteToRepair flag going false (set at the top of finished(), before the mode-restart happens) instead of isActive(), and explicitly calls stopRoute() to cancel any stray AD reactivation once the flag clears. WorkflowExecutor's completion poll now calls isRefuelRepairComplete for STEP_REFUEL/STEP_REPAIR instead of isRouteComplete.

bugs.root_cause: ADIntegration:getRearAttachedObject() picked vehicle:getAttachedImplements()[1] and treated it as 'the rear-attached implement', but getAttachedImplements() returns ALL directly attached implements in attacherJoint order, not spatial front-to-rear order. bugs.fix: Rewrote getRearAttachedObject to resolve 'rear' by world position instead of list order, mirroring AD's own convention in AutoDrive.getVehicleLeadingEdge (AutoDrive.worldToLocal diffZ sign): iterate all attached implements, compute each one's z-offset relative to the vehicle via getWorldTranslation + AutoDrive.worldToLocal, and pick the implement with the most-negative diffZ (furthest behind). Implements with diffZ >= 0 (front-attached) are ignored. If nothing is behind the vehicle, correctly falls through to the vehicle's own parkDestination.

User confirmed (after being asked directly) that the park position was set via AD's own UI while the trailer itself was the selected/active tool - AD's real model has NO front/rear concept at all: AutoDriveVehicleData:onEnterVehicle/onSelect show the marker id is written onto whichever object (vehicle or implement) was selected in-game when 'Set Park Position' was pressed. The geometry guess was therefore solving a problem that doesn't exist in AD's data model, and evidently had a sign or structural mismatch that excluded the correctly-configured trailer.
bugs.fix: Removed getRearAttachedObject and its geometry/diffZ logic entirely. getVehicleParkDestinationId now iterates every directly-attached implement (vehicle:getAttachedImplements(), no recursive chain-walking) in attach order and returns the first one with a valid, non-stale advd.parkDestination, falling back to the vehicle's own only if none of the implements have one configured. Matches AD's actual 'whichever object was selected' semantics with no geometry involved. Rewrote AutoDriveIntegration_spec.lua's getVehicleParkDestinationId/startParkRoute tests around implementParkIds (ordered list, no spatial mocking needed) and removed the getRearAttachedObject describe block. Also updated user-facing strings ('rear-attached implement' -> 'any attached implement') in WorkflowExecutor.lua, WorkflowManager.lua, and website/docs (troubleshooting.md, step-types.md).

bugs.error_message: Workflow editor 'Cancel' does not revert changes: added/removed/reordered/edited steps, renames and adSettings all persist and get written on the next saveWorkflows()
bugs.root_cause: setWorkflow stored the live workflow table directly, so every step operation (table.insert/table.remove/in-place swap, onNameEnterPressed, onClickADSettings) mutated the real object immediately. onClickCancel only skipped WorkflowManager:saveWorkflows(), so the in-memory mutations survived and were persisted by any later save trigger (game save, HUD drag, delete confirm). onClickAddSupportStep additionally wrote through WorkflowManager:addSupportStep(), which resolves the workflow by id from WorkflowManager.workflows.
bugs.fix: Added a file-local deepCopy(); setWorkflow now keeps the live table as self.sourceWorkflow and edits a copy in self.workflow. New commitToSource() writes name/steps/adSettings back IN PLACE (a running execution holds a reference via activeData.workflow, so the table identity must be preserved) and is called only from onClickSave. onClickCancel clears the buffer. onClickAddSupportStep appends to the buffer instead of calling addSupportStep. New tests/specs/WMEditorDialog_spec.lua (24 tests) covers commit vs discard, nested-table independence, in-place mutation and post-commit aliasing.

Tagged the two support call sites in WMEditorDialog (onClickEditStep support branch, onClickAddSupportStep). For workflows already saved with a marker sub-step, the executor support branch now treats isMarkerStepType as a pass-through (onStepCompleted + warning) instead of handleStepError. bugs.error_message: Courseplay course list in the WM editor is incomplete / a saved course fails to load ('Could not load course') depending on which folder the player last opened in Courseplay's own course manager
bugs.root_cause: Both the enumeration side (CPCoursesLoader:extractCoursesFromFileSystem) and the load side (CPIntegration:loadCourseFromStorage) started from 'currentDirectoryView or rootDirectoryView'. currentDirectoryView tracks Courseplay's own GUI navigation, so (a) only courses under that folder were listed, (b) their names were recorded relative to it (bare 'Field B' instead of 'Farm2/Field B'), and (c) a stored path like 'Farm1/Course' was then looked up as a child of whatever folder CP happened to be in, so navigateToFolder failed. The two sides could disagree because CP's navigation state changed between authoring a workflow and running it.
bugs.fix: Both sides now resolve from rootDirectoryView (currentDirectoryView kept only as a fallback when no root view exists, and in the loader only when the root walk yields zero courses). Added CPIntegration:findCourseEntry, which resolves the stored path from the root and then falls back to a depth-limited recursive search by base name, so course names recorded under the old behaviour (and courses moved between folders since) still load. Extracted CPIntegration:isDirectoryEntry/getEntryName/getSubView/getViewEntries/findEntryByName/findEntryByNameRecursive; isDirectoryEntry handles isDirectory-as-field, isDirectory-as-method and getIsDirectory(), because the loader previously only handled the method shape and would have enumerated folder names as courses now that scanning always walks the tree from the root. collectCoursesFromDirectoryView also resolves a subfolder's view via getSubView before recursing instead of recursing on the raw entry. The ~120-line load-attempt chain moved verbatim into CPIntegration:tryLoadEntry with no semantic change. New specs: CourseplayIntegration_spec.lua (27) and CourseplayCoursesLoader_spec.lua (13).

bugs.error_message: Workflow does not continue after loading a savegame that was taken while a Courseplay step was driving; pressing Resume logs "Courseplay never started for workflow X" and silently skips the field work step.
bugs.root_cause: Courseplay deliberately never auto-resumes (CpAIFieldWorker overwrites the base-game AIFieldWorker#isActive to false at save time), so WM's 10s autoResumeUntil window - which only ATTACHES monitoring to a job that restarted itself - could never catch a CP step and the workflow stayed PAUSED forever. On manual Resume the post-load branch of resumeWorkflow assumed AD/CP had already auto-started, so it set waitingForCompletion=true with cpWasRunning=false; the completion poll then hit the "not cpRunning and not cpWasRunning" branch and marked the step complete. Additionally CP only writes its own #rememberedWpIx on a clean strategy stop, never mid-drive, so even an active restart would have fallen back to waypoint 1 and re-driven the whole field.
bugs.fix: WM now captures the resume waypoint itself at save time: WorkflowManagerSpec:saveToXMLFile writes #cpWasRunning and #cpResumeWaypoint (from new CPIntegration:getResumeWaypointIx, which reads the live strategy via vehicle:getCpDriveStrategy():getBestWaypointToContinueFieldWork() and falls back to getCpLastRememberedWaypointIx). onPostLoad restores them as cpWasRunningAtSave/cpResumeWaypoint. New WMExecutor:resumeCourseplayAfterLoad re-issues the start when the autoResumeUntil window expires and from resumeWorkflow's post-load branch; it uses getCurrentStep so support vehicles resolve their own CP sub-step. startCourseplayStep seeds the waypoint via CPIntegration:setResumeWaypointIx AFTER the course load (loading a course clears CP's remembered index) and forces startAtFirst=false. With no recorded waypoint the workflow stays PAUSED and warns, and keeps cpWasRunningAtSave set so repeated Resume presses cannot fall through to the step-skipping path. Also removed the dead, mislabelled startAtNearest branch in CPIntegration:startFieldWork.

bugs.error_message: OPEN / NOT FIXED - after a savegame load, a restored SUPPORT vehicle can auto-resume with the wrong currentStepType.
bugs.root_cause: The auto-resume poll reads the step as workflow.steps[activeData.currentStep], i.e. the MAIN vehicle step list. For a support vehicle the live step is workflow.steps[main.currentStep].support[activeData.currentSupportStep]. If AD or CP is detected running inside the 10s window, activeData.currentStepType is set from the main step instead of the support sub-step, so completion detection afterwards runs through the wrong per-step-type branch (e.g. AD route polling for what is really a CP sub-step). WMExecutor:getCurrentStep already resolves both roles correctly.
bugs.fix: NOT APPLIED - documented only. A KNOWN ISSUE comment marks the line. The fix is to use self:getCurrentStep(activeData) there, but it also changes the AutoDrive auto-resume path for support vehicles, so it needs its own test pass and was kept out of the Courseplay resume-after-load change. New code added in that change (WMExecutor:resumeCourseplayAfterLoad) already uses getCurrentStep and has a regression test covering the support-vehicle case.

bugs.error_message: After creating a workflow and closing the WM dialogs, keyboard and mouse are sometimes dead. Log: 'Tried reverting to input context [] which is not defined. Current context [TEXT_INPUT]' then 'Tried reverting to input context [TEXT_INPUT] ... Current context [DIALOG_WMStepDialog]'
bugs.root_cause: The step and AD/CP settings dialogs were opened ON TOP of the still-open editor (and the settings dialog on top of the main dialog). FS25 pushes one input context per open dialog; in the nested dialog a focused TextInput records an EMPTY previous context, so TextInputElement:onFocusLeave -> revertContext fails and TEXT_INPUT is never popped. Every later push/pop is then off by one: the next dialog stores TEXT_INPUT as its previous context, that temporary context is already destroyed, and after the whole chain closes the game stays parked in DIALOG_WMStepDialog - a context with no gameplay bindings. WMHud then releases the mouse cursor on the last onDialogClosed, so keyboard AND mouse are gone. Intermittent because it needs a text field (target search / workflow name) to be focused and then clicked away from. Control case in the same log: the editor's nameInput, used while the editor was the ONLY open dialog, reverted cleanly with no warning.
bugs.fix: Never stack two WM dialogs. WMEditorDialog:suspendForChildDialog() closes the editor (carrying the uncommitted nameInput text into the edit buffer first) before showStepDialog/showADSettingsDialog, and resumeAfterChildDialog() -> WorkflowManager:reopenEditorDialog() re-shows it from the child's callback (all paths, including cancel). WMMainDialog:onClickADSettings closes before showing and reopens in the callback. Same sequential pattern Main->Editor and the start/leader/mode chain already use.

bugs.error_message: tests/specs/CourseplayIntegration_spec.lua:454: attempt to index field 'is_not' (a nil value)
bugs.root_cause: The hand-rolled assert table in tests/run_tests.lua has assert.are_not.equal and assert.is_not_nil, but NO assert.is_not.equal - it is a busted-shaped subset, not busted.
bugs.fix: Used assert.is_true(x ~= y) instead. Available negatives: assert.are_not.equal, assert.is_not_nil, assert.is_false, assert.is_nil.

bugs.error_message: Mod unusable without AutoDrive: every start refused with "Vehicle 'X' needs AutoDrive + Courseplay", even for workflows made only of Courseplay steps.
bugs.root_cause: isVehicleValid hardcoded `return hasAutoDrive and hasCP`, so resolveStartTarget rejected any vehicle without vehicle.ad / spec_autoDrive - which is every vehicle when AutoDrive is not installed. Everything else (ADIntegration entry points, the editor's cache load) already degraded gracefully, so this single gate was the only blocker.
bugs.fix: Added WorkflowManager:workflowNeedsAutoDrive(workflow) (scans steps and support sub-steps for isAutoDriveTrackedStepType) and made isVehicleValid(vehicle, workflow) require CP always and AD only when the workflow needs it. A nil workflow still requires AD. resolveStartTarget passes the workflow and picks the wm_warning_incompatible_vehicle_cp message when only CP is needed.

bugs.error_message: WMStepDialog spec: 'hides the four AD-driven types when AutoDrive is not installed' - Expected 3, got 4
bugs.root_cause: getStepTypes keeps the step's CURRENT type listed even when filtered out (so legacy data can be converted), and setStep defaults a NEW step to stepType="autodrive". Without AutoDrive the new-step default therefore re-added AutoDrive to the dropdown, and confirming would have saved an unrunnable AD step.
bugs.fix: setStep now defaults a new step to STEP_COURSEPLAY/"fieldwork" when WMStepDialog:isAutoDriveAvailable() is false, keeping AutoDrive/"drive" otherwise.

bugs.error_message: Error: Could not find motion path effect mesh for settings (Class: 'CutterMotionPathEffect', numRows: 32, rowLength: 42, fruitType 'MAIZE', growthState '7', fillType 'MAIZE') / MotionPathEffectManager.lua:514: attempt to index nil with 'speedScale'
bugs.root_cause: The Cressoni 14m grain header attached to the LEXION 8900 declares <motionPathEffect numRows="32" rowLength="42"> (grainheader beltXArray). The NDL map registers CUTTER effect meshes for MAIZE growthState 7 only in cornheader/maizeheader dimensions (6x5, 6x20, 12x26, 20x36, 6x8, 12x8, 20x8 - see FS25_NDL/xml/cutterEffects.xml). When the combine's cutting area covers maize, the engine looks up a 32x42 MAIZE mesh, finds none, and MotionPathEffectManager indexes the nil result. Purely cosmetic/base-game; WorkflowManager has zero motion-path/cutter code.
bugs.fix: No WM change. Harvest maize with a maize/corn header (e.g. the Capello Diamant 8) instead of the Cressoni 14m grain header, or report to the header mod author. Do NOT re-investigate this from the WM side.

bugs.error_message: It seems like there are some input bindings missing in that dialog (WMEditorDialog)
bugs.root_cause: WMEditorDialog only had keyboard actions for Delete/Move Up/Move Down. The New step, Edit step and Add Support Step buttons had no InputAction assigned and no registered action event, so they were mouse-only and showed no key glyph, unlike the equivalent buttons in WMMainDialog.
bugs.fix: Added WM_GUI_NEW (KEY_n), WM_GUI_EDIT (KEY_e) and WM_GUI_ADD_SUPPORT (KEY_s) to modDesc.xml actions + inputBinding and to both translation files (action_/input_ pairs). WMEditorDialog:onOpen now calls setInputAction on all six step buttons; registerInputEvents registers all six; new onInputAddStep/onInputEditStep/onInputAddSupportStep handlers mirror the existing disabled-guard pattern.

bugs.error_message: Audit follow-up: which other key bindings are missing? (WMMainDialog New/Edit; WMLeaderVehicleSelectDialog No Leader; WMModeSelectDialog Run as Support)
bugs.root_cause: WMMainDialog bound only Delete/Start/Stop/AD-Settings, leaving New and Edit mouse-only. The secondary choice in the two 3-button dialogs ('No Leader', 'Run as Support') had no id attribute in its GUI XML at all, so Lua could not reference the button to bind it; neither dialog had registerInputEvents.
bugs.fix: WMMainDialog: setInputAction + registered events + onInputNew/onInputEdit reusing the existing WM_GUI_NEW/WM_GUI_EDIT actions. Added WM_GUI_NO_LEADER (KEY_space) and WM_GUI_RUN_SUPPORT (KEY_f) to modDesc + both translations; gave the two buttons ids (noLeaderButton, supportButton) and added the register/unregister/handler trio to both dialogs.

bugs.error_message: The edit key (e) does not work in any dialog; changing the assignment did not fix it
bugs.root_cause: Gui:registerMenuInput registers the menu navigation actions (Gui.NAV_ACTIONS) in the dialog input context. KEY_e is MENU_PAGE_NEXT, so the colliding WM_GUI_EDIT binding never fired. The player's rebind went to KEY_space (MENU_ACTIVATE), also menu-owned. The handler code was correct: New/Delete use the identical pattern and work.
bugs.fix: WM_GUI_EDIT default KEY_e -> KEY_t (user's choice). Added ModDescInputBindings_spec pinning Edit=KEY_t and forbidding KEY_q/KEY_e on WM_GUI_* actions. Saved profile bindings override modDesc defaults, so existing players must rebind in Options. Follow-up: the user confirmed WM_GUI_STOP on KEY_x (MENU_EXTRA_1) was dead too, so it moved to KEY_k and KEY_x joined the spec's forbidden list. D (MENU_EXTRA_3) is left as is pending an in-game test.
Changed to 's MENU_EXTRA_1 owns X inside every dialog. -->
